statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-107655 (GHSA-58wv-9ffm-5w78): in OpenPrinting CUPS through 2.4.20, an embedded %cupsJobTicket: comment in a PostScript or PDF job can replace the request's attributes-natural-language attribute with a keyword, and cupsdContinueJob() then dereferences a NULL pointer when the job starts, so a client allowed to submit jobs can crash cupsd. Upstream fixed it after 2.4.20 by refusing those attributes in job tickets and adding a JobTicketComments directive to cups-files.conf, disabled by default: https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/security/advisories/GHSA-58wv-9ffm-5w78, https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/commit/25d68309b1af89c4b003f27f56ab0f8e7a189ea3. Debian lists trixie's 2.4.10-3+deb13u2 as vulnerable and fixes it in 2.4.20-1 for unstable: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-107655. DHI publishes four rebuilds of Debian's cups 2.4.10-3+deb13u2 for Debian 13 (amd64 and arm64). Checked each of their cups-daemon packages: the Debian changelog of the first two does not list CVE-2026-107655 and their /usr/sbin/cupsd has no JobTicketComments directive; the third and fourth record the backport of the upstream fix in their changelog and their cupsd recognises JobTicketComments. The third rebuild is the fixed version in this range; every earlier build, including the earlier rebuilds no longer in the repository, is affected.
